text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 2 in history.
1187 - Saladin, the Sultan of Syria, captured Jerusalem from the Christians.

1452 - Richard III, King of England, born. Usurped power in 1483 after the death of Edward IV. The throne rightly belonged to Edward V, but he and his brother disappeared and some believe Richard had them murdered.
1608 - The first telescope was demonstrated by Hans Lippershey of Middelburg.
1836 - Charles Darwin returned to Falmouth, England, aboard HMS Beagle, after a five-year exploration of the southern oceans.
1847 - Paul Von Hindenburg, German statesman and soldier, born. As a Field Marshal, he led the German land forces during World War One and was President of Germany from 1925-34.
1851 - Ferdinand Foch born. He became Marshal of France and commander of Allied forces during the final stages of World War One.
1852 - Sir William Ramsay, Scottish chemist who discovered Helium, Xenon, Neon, Argon, Radon and Krypton, born.

1869 - Mahatma Ghandi (Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi) born. Considered the Father of India, he led the nationalist movement against British rule. Renowned for his advocacy of non-violent civil disobedience to achieve political aims.
1870 - In a plebiscite, the Papal States voted for union with Italy. The country's capital moved from Florence to Rome.
1890 - Groucho Marx, best-known of the Marx brothers, born as Julius Henry Marx. Starred in a series of films with his brothers including "Night at the Opera" and "A Day at the Races".
1895 - Bud Abbott, half of the U.S. comedy duo Abbott and Costello, born as William Abbott.
1901 - The first submarine commissioned by the British Navy as launched from Barrow.
1901 - Roy Campbell, one of the most distinguished poets to emerge from South Africa, born.
1904 - Graham Greene, British novelist and playwright notably of "Our Man in Havana", "The Honorary Consul" and "The Third Man", born.
1904 - Lal Bahadur Shastri born. He was an Indian politician who became a member of Mahatma Gandhi's non-cooperation movement and was prime minister from June 1964 until his death in January 1966.
1921 - Robert Runcie, British clergyman and Archbishop of Canterbury from 1980-91, born.
1935 - Italian forces invaded Abyssinia. After Italy's defeat at Adua in 1896, Mussolini wanted revenge and also had imperialist ambitions in Africa. The Italian occupation lasted until 1941.
1942 - British Cruiser Curacao, escorting the Queen Mary across the Atlantic, was struck by the liner during confusion over the sighting of a submarine. The Curacao sank with the loss of 338 lives.
1958 - The Republic of Guinea in West Africa achieved independence from France.
1972 - Denmark voted by 63.4 per cent to 36.6 to join the European Economic Community.
1973 - Paavo Nurmi, Finnish long-distance runner who dominated the sport in the 1920s, died.
1985 - Rock Hudson, U.S. film star best known for his roles in "Giant" and with film star Doris Day in "Pillow Talk", died of AIDS.
1990 - 127 people were killed when a hijacked Chinese jet crashed into two parked planes at Canton Airport following an explosion on board.
1992 - Brazilian President Fernando Collor was stripped of power by congress and warned he would face an impeachment trial. Vice-president Itamar Franco was put in charge.
